name: Indian peafowl
fact: India's national bird. Males fan out their train in the monsoon to attract mates.

name: House sparrow
fact: Once everywhere in Punjab villages, now declining in many cities. Leaving small water bowls out helps.

name: Rose-ringed parakeet
fact: Loud green parrots that nest in tree holes and old walls, often in big noisy flocks.

name: Hoopoe
fact: Spots a crest it raises when alarmed, and probes lawns and fields for insects with a long curved bill.

name: Common myna
fact: Very social and a great mimic. Usually walks rather than hops.

name: Asian koel
fact: The rising 'ku-oo' call you hear in summer is the male. They lay eggs in crow nests.

name: Black drongo
fact: Farmers like it: it perches on wires and fence posts and snaps up crop-eating insects.

name: Indian roller
fact: Flashes bright blue wings in flight. Named for its rolling display flight.

name: Shisham
fact: Dalbergia sissoo, a common roadside and canal-bank tree in Punjab with valuable, durable timber.

name: Neem
fact: Azadirachta indica. Leaves and twigs have long been used in traditional hygiene and as a natural pest repellent.

name: Peepal
fact: Ficus religiosa. Heart-shaped leaves with a long drip tip; sacred in several traditions and often planted near villages.

name: Banyan
fact: Ficus benghalensis. Grows aerial roots that become new trunks, so one tree can spread very wide.

name: Kikar
fact: Vachellia nilotica (babul). Thorny, tough tree of dry areas with feathery leaves and yellow puffball flowers.

name: Eucalyptus
fact: Widely planted along Punjab roads and field edges. Fast-growing but thirsty, using a lot of groundwater.

name: Mustard
fact: Yellow winter fields of sarson are iconic in Punjab. Sarson da saag is the classic dish.

name: Marigold
fact: Genda. Easy to grow, used in garlands, and often planted in gardens to deter some pests.
